title: Altinn Studio — Designer
description: Altinn Studio Designer (service studio-designer) in the Studio environments. Traffic, errors and latency of its requests, its outgoing calls by host and its SignalR connections come from its HTTP and SignalR metrics (altinn-studio-metrics), with links from the panels to matching traces. Below them, for triage, lists of individual failed and slow requests, failed background jobs and failed outgoing calls, each linked to its trace, with breakdowns, from Designer's spans through altinn-studio-traces-logsql (LogsQL). Tail sampling keeps every trace with an error or over 1 s, so those lists are complete, but only 10 % of the other traces, so counts and latency of all requests come from the metrics. Datasource UIDs are pinned, matching the other Altinn Studio dashboards. Rates use increase_pure() over $__rate_interval divided by its length rather than rate(): VictoriaMetrics' rate() takes a new series' first sample as its baseline, so a first error on a route, status or error type would never show. Instance markers come from altinn.instance.start_time: blue marks the earliest retained start per environment/version over 90 days, orange marks each process start in range. Rollbacks to a retained version have only new-instance markers. History is limited by metric retention and successfully exported samples. Instances reporting counts processes with a sample in the last minute at the range end; it does not measure readiness. These features need the service metric rollout before they show production data.

list.name: filters
list.label: Filters
list.description: Filters the trace tables (LogsQL) on any span field, such as span_attr:altinn.service_owner, span_attr:altinn.app or span_attr:enduser.id. The metric panels have no such labels and are not filtered.

list.name: Deploys (first start of version)
list.textFormat: {{deployment.environment.name}}. Earliest retained process start for this version (90d history). Rollbacks to a retained version do not add a deploy dot.

list.name: Restarts / new instances
list.textFormat: {{deployment.environment.name}} · {{service.version}} · {{service.instance.id}} · pod {{k8s.pod.uid}}. Includes rollout, restart and scale-up; telemetry cannot distinguish their cause.

panels.title: Instances reporting
panels.description: Processes with at least one instance start-time sample in the preceding minute, evaluated at the dashboard range end. Counts processes exporting telemetry, not Kubernetes readiness or health. Replaced processes remain for up to one minute; missing telemetry stays No data. Requires the instance metric service rollout.

panels.title: Requests per second
panels.description: Requests Designer served, from its HTTP server metrics (http.server.request.duration). SignalR hub connections and health checks are not counted; hub negotiation and failed connection attempts are.

panels.title: Server errors
panels.description: Share of Designer requests that failed with a 5xx. Client errors (4xx) are in Client and server errors by status code.

panels.title: p95 latency
panels.description: 95th percentile duration of all Designer requests. The histogram's buckets end at 10 s, so a value of 10 s means 10 s or more; Slowest requests below has the actual durations.

panels.title: Requests in flight
panels.description: Requests Designer is handling right now, summed over its pods (http.server.active_requests, sampled at each export). Rising in-flight requests without more traffic mean requests wait, such as on Gitea or a lock.

panels.title: Responses by status class
panels.description: Designer requests per second by status class, one line per class (not stacked). Most 2xx is gitea-proxy's userinfo check for every request to Gitea, a 204 when the caller has no Studio session; Routes below shows each route. Select a series to search the traces in that class; tail sampling keeps every trace with an error or over 1 s, but only 10 % of the others.

panels.title: Client and server errors by status code
panels.description: Designer requests per second that ended in a 4xx or 5xx, by status code, one line per code (not stacked), so the small series are not hidden by the successful traffic. 499 (grey) is a client that closed the connection before the response. Select a series to search the traces with that status.

panels.title: Latency
panels.description: Duration of all Designer requests: median, 95th and 99th percentile. The buckets end at 10 s, so the percentiles cannot show more than 10 s; longer requests (clone, pull, push, deploy) are in Slowest requests. Select a series to search traces over 1 s.

panels.title: Routes
panels.description: Every route over the dashboard's time range: requests, server errors (5xx) and their share, and the median and 95th percentile duration (at most 10 s, where the buckets end). (none) is requests that matched no endpoint, such as static files and unknown paths. Sorted by requests; select a column header to sort by another. Select a route to search its traces, or its server errors to search its failed traces.

panels.title: Outgoing calls by host
panels.description: HTTP calls per second from Designer by host (server.address): Gitea (altinn-repositories), Azure DevOps, the runtime environments' platform APIs and others, from the HTTP client metrics (http.client.request.duration).

panels.title: Outgoing call latency (p95)
panels.description: 95th percentile duration of Designer's outgoing HTTP calls by host. The buckets end at 10 s.

panels.title: Failed outgoing calls by host
panels.description: Outgoing HTTP calls per second that failed with a 5xx or without a response, by host and error.type (the status code, or the exception type, such as a timeout or a refused connection). 4xx responses are left out, as in Recent failed outgoing calls: Designer handles most of them. Select a series to search the failed calls' traces.

panels.title: Active SignalR connections
panels.description: Open SignalR connections to Designer's hubs (preview, sync, entity and alert updates, assistant) by transport, summed over its pods. Connections falling back from web_sockets to long_polling or server_sent_events suggest WebSockets fail on the way in.

panels.title: SignalR connections closed
panels.description: SignalR connections closed per second by how they ended (signalr.connection.status): normal_closure, timeout (the client stopped responding) or app_shutdown (a Designer pod stopped). A connection's duration is the length of a session, so it says nothing about latency and is not shown.

panels.title: Failed requests (traces)
panels.description: Failed Designer requests per second, counted from server spans with status error (a 5xx or an unhandled exception). Tail sampling keeps every failed trace, so the count is complete; each dot is an example trace to open.

panels.title: Failures by request and error type
panels.description: Failed Designer requests over the time range, by request (method and route) and error.type: the exception type for an unhandled exception, or the status code for a 5xx response without one. Complete, as tail sampling keeps every trace with an error.

targets.expr: {resource_attr:service.name="studio-designer"} "resource_attr:deployment.environment.name":$env kind:2 status_code:2 | stats by (name, "span_attr:error.type") count() failures, count_uniq("span_attr:enduser.id") users

panels.title: Recent failed requests
panels.description: The latest 200 failed Designer requests: server spans with status error, which ASP.NET Core sets on a 5xx response or an unhandled exception. 4xx responses are not errors. Error type is error.type; Exception message is the first exception recorded on the span. Service owner, app and user are Designer's own attributes on the request span, set where the route or the login has them. Select a trace ID to open the trace.

targets.expr: {resource_attr:service.name="studio-designer"} "resource_attr:deployment.environment.name":$env kind:2 status_code:2 | sort by (_time desc) limit 200 | fields _time, name, "span_attr:http.response.status_code", "span_attr:error.type", "event:event_attr:exception.message:0", "span_attr:altinn.service_owner", "span_attr:altinn.app", "span_attr:enduser.id", duration, trace_id | rename trace_id as trace

panels.title: Slow requests by request
panels.description: Designer requests that took more than 1 s, by request (method and route): how many, and the median and slowest. Tail sampling keeps every trace over 1 s, so these are complete; latency of all requests is in the HTTP server metrics.

targets.expr: {resource_attr:service.name="studio-designer"} "resource_attr:deployment.environment.name":$env kind:2 duration:>1s | stats by (name) count() slow, quantile(0.5, duration) median, max(duration) slowest

panels.title: Slow requests by service owner and app
panels.description: Designer requests that took more than 1 s, by service owner and app (empty for requests outside an app, such as the dashboard). Complete, as tail sampling keeps every trace over 1 s.

targets.expr: {resource_attr:service.name="studio-designer"} "resource_attr:deployment.environment.name":$env kind:2 duration:>1s | stats by ("span_attr:altinn.service_owner", "span_attr:altinn.app") count() slow, count_uniq("span_attr:enduser.id") users, max(duration) slowest

panels.title: Slowest requests
panels.description: The 200 slowest Designer requests over 1 s in the time range, slowest first, including those that succeeded. Select a trace ID to open the trace and see where the time went (git operations, Gitea and other outgoing calls, the database).

targets.expr: {resource_attr:service.name="studio-designer"} "resource_attr:deployment.environment.name":$env kind:2 duration:>1s | sort by (duration desc) limit 200 | fields _time, name, "span_attr:http.response.status_code", "span_attr:error.type", "event:event_attr:exception.message:0", "span_attr:altinn.service_owner", "span_attr:altinn.app", "span_attr:enduser.id", duration, trace_id | rename trace_id as trace

panels.title: Failed background jobs
panels.description: Quartz job runs that failed with an exception: the job's root span, named execute <job type>, with status error. Message is the exception message the Quartz instrumentation puts in the span status, and Exception its type. Tail sampling keeps every trace with an error.

targets.expr: {resource_attr:service.name="studio-designer"} "resource_attr:deployment.environment.name":$env name:="execute "* status_code:2 | sort by (_time desc) limit 200 | fields _time, name, "event:event_attr:exception.type:0", status_message, "span_attr:altinn.service_owner", "span_attr:altinn.app", duration, trace_id | rename trace_id as trace

panels.title: Recent failed outgoing calls
panels.description: Outgoing HTTP calls from Designer (to Gitea, Azure DevOps, the runtime environments and others) that failed with a 5xx or without a response (Status empty, error.type the exception type). 4xx responses are left out: the HTTP client marks them as errors, but Designer handles most of them, such as a 404 for a file missing in Gitea; one it doesn't handle fails the request, which Recent failed requests shows. URL is redacted where it carries secrets. Select a trace ID to see which request or job made the call.

targets.expr: {resource_attr:service.name="studio-designer"} "resource_attr:deployment.environment.name":$env kind:3 status_code:2 !"span_attr:http.response.status_code":4* | sort by (_time desc) limit 200 | fields _time, "span_attr:http.request.method", "span_attr:server.address", "span_attr:url.full", "span_attr:http.response.status_code", "span_attr:error.type", duration, trace_id | rename trace_id as trace
